heuristics.rule: Use Canadian-specific salary sources (Robert Half Canada, Glassdoor CA) — never US sources — when negotiating Canadian offers
heuristics.condition: When negotiating a salary offer for a tech role in Canada...
heuristics.action: ...anchor to Robert Half Canada ranges and Glassdoor CA medians, not levels.fyi US or Glassdoor US
heuristics.because: US benchmarks are 25–40% higher in USD terms and will either cause you to anchor too high (seeming out of touch) or too low (leaving money on the table at Canadian ceiling)

heuristics.rule: At Canadian tech employers, negotiate signing bonus first — not base salary — because it is the most flexible component
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian employer says 'the band is set' on base salary...
heuristics.action: ...shift negotiation to signing bonus rather than continuing to push on base
heuristics.because: Canadian offers have narrower negotiating bands (3–10%) than US (10–20%), and employers at established companies often genuinely cannot move the base but have more discretion on signing

heuristics.rule: When comparing a Calgary offer to a Toronto/Vancouver offer, add 8–12% to the Calgary gross salary before comparing take-home
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a tech job offer in Calgary (Alberta) vs. Ontario or BC...
heuristics.action: ...adjust for Alberta's zero provincial income tax, which increases effective take-home by approximately 8–12% on the same gross
heuristics.because: A CAD $130,000 gross in Calgary yields materially more take-home than the same gross in Toronto or Vancouver due to the absence of provincial income tax

heuristics.rule: At FAANG Canada (Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Shopify), expect total comp to significantly exceed base — negotiate RSU grants and refresh schedules, not just base
heuristics.condition: When negotiating at a large tech employer in Canada that offers RSUs...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate and negotiate total comp including RSU vesting schedules, not just base salary
heuristics.because: Senior SWE total comp at FAANG Canada ($175K–$260K+ CAD) can exceed base ($145K–$185K) by 30–50%, making base-only negotiation leave significant value uncaptured

heuristics.rule: Discount Montreal salaries by 15–25% versus Toronto when comparing raw numbers, then partially offset for lower cost of living
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a Montreal tech offer against a Toronto benchmark...
heuristics.action: ...recognize the posted salary will be 15–25% lower than Toronto equivalents, but factor in lower Montreal cost of living before concluding it's a worse deal
heuristics.because: Montreal's lower salary market is structural (bilingual requirements, different labor market) but cost of living partially compensates, so direct gross salary comparison overstates the real gap

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Salary benchmarks vary 10–25% across Canadian cities, and Alberta's no-provincial-income-tax rule changes effective take-home independently of gross salary
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare gross offer to city-specific benchmarks (Toronto/Vancouver as baseline); for Calgary/Edmonton add 8–12% take-home premium; for Montreal discount 15–25% but adjust for COL

decision_factors.factor: Employer type: FAANG Canada vs. mid-tier tech vs. enterprise
decision_factors.why_it_matters: FAANG Canada pays materially more in total comp (especially RSUs) than the broad market — mid-tier Canadian tech often pays near Robert Half ranges with no equity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether offer includes RSUs; compare to FAANG Canada benchmarks (Amazon, Google, Shopify) vs. Robert Half ranges for non-FAANG

decision_factors.why_it_matters: For senior roles, RSUs can add 30–50% above base salary; not negotiating or understanding them means treating a $170K total comp role as a $145K base role
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request full RSU grant amount, vesting cliff, annual refresh rate; compare to role-level benchmarks at FAANG Canada

decision_factors.factor: Pay transparency legislation (BC and Ontario, Jan 2026)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Posted salary ranges will become mandatory, removing information asymmetry and allowing candidates to see the full band before negotiating
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the job posting already includes a salary range (early compliers exist); if not, ask recruiter for the band directly

decision_factors.factor: Canadian vs. US immigration status and path to PR
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The Canada–US comp gap is severe at FAANG level (senior SWE: $161K USD Canada vs. $400K USD US FAANG), but US H-1B uncertainty and 134-year India-born green card wait changes the real expected value calculation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For international candidates: compare expected compensation over 5–10 year horizon including immigration stability premium; Canadian PR achievable in 1–2 years vs. H-1B uncertainty

decision_factors.why_it_matters: RRSP matching is a form of deferred compensation not captured in base salary; it affects total comp comparison across employers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request specifics on RRSP match percentage and vesting; include in total comp calculation alongside base and equity

decision_factors.factor: Years of experience relative to role level benchmarks
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian salary bands are meaningfully different by seniority level (junior $65K–$95K vs. senior $120K–$165K); being mis-leveled down costs $25K–$40K annually
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Match your YOE (0–3, 3–6, 6–10) to published Robert Half Canada ranges for your role; flag if offer falls below median for your experience tier

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a Canadian tech role over a US FAANG offer
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: At senior levels, the total compensation gap is severe — a senior SWE earns $150K–$220K CAD ($110K–$161K USD) in Canada vs. $250K–$400K USD at US FAANG. Over a 5-year career the gap can exceed $500K–$1M USD in forgone earnings.
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: High-performing senior engineers who qualify for US FAANG roles but choose Canada for immigration stability or lifestyle reasons

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Negotiating with US salary data in a Canadian interview process
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: You appear out of touch with Canadian market norms, which signals poor market research to the recruiter and can damage your candidacy even if your target number is individually reasonable
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students or recent US-based candidates who apply to Canadian roles without recalibrating their salary expectations to the Canadian market

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Focusing negotiation only on base salary in Canada
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The most movable component (signing bonus) goes unasked, and the highest-value component at FAANG Canada (RSU grants) goes unoptimized — both represent more negotiable upside than base
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Junior and mid-level candidates negotiating their first Canadian tech offer, who default to base salary as the only lever

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Taking a Montreal role because the salary looks close to Toronto after reading the job posting
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Montreal salaries are structurally 15–25% below Toronto; bilingual requirements can also constrain future mobility within the Montreal market for non-French speakers
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates relocating to Montreal from other provinces or countries who don't adjust for the structural salary discount

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting the first offer at a Canadian established company after being told 'the band is set'
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The signing bonus — which is expected to be asked for at Canadian tech companies — is left entirely on the table, representing $5K–$20K+ in immediately accessible compensation
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: First-time negotiators who take 'the band is set' as a signal that all negotiation is closed

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Comparing a Calgary gross salary offer directly to a Toronto gross salary offer
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Alberta's absence of provincial income tax means the Calgary offer is worth 8–12% more in take-home than the identical gross in Toronto — ignoring this makes Calgary look worse than it is
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates choosing between Alberta and Ontario/BC roles who evaluate offers by gross salary alone

failure_patterns.pattern: Anchoring Canadian salary negotiation to US market data from levels.fyi or Glassdoor US
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Most widely available English-language salary content is US-centric; candidates assume it's globally applicable or don't know Canadian-specific sources exist
failure_patterns.consequence: Either anchoring 25–40% too high (seeming delusional to Canadian recruiters, losing offers) or using US data to validate accepting a below-market Canadian offer
warning_signs: Candidate cites levels.fyi numbers without specifying 'Canada' data
Candidate quotes USD figures when discussing CAD-denominated roles

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating Robert Half Canada ranges as the ceiling rather than the floor for FAANG Canada negotiation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Robert Half ranges represent the broad Canadian market including non-tech employers; candidates don't realize FAANG Canada (Amazon, Google, Shopify) pays 20–40% above these ranges
failure_patterns.consequence: Underanchoring at major tech companies — e.g., targeting $138K CAD for a senior SWE role where Amazon Canada pays $145K–$170K base and Google Canada pays $155K–$185K
warning_signs: Candidate treats Robert Half midpoint as the target rather than the floor
Candidate doesn't distinguish between FAANG Canada and general market benchmarks

failure_patterns.pattern: Not asking about signing bonus because the base salary feels acceptable
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates conflate 'I'm happy with the base' with 'negotiation is complete'; don't know that signing bonus is expected to be requested at Canadian tech companies
failure_patterns.consequence: Leaving $5K–$20K+ in immediately vested compensation unclaimed simply by not asking
warning_signs: Candidate verbally accepts offer on the spot without asking about signing bonus
Candidate says 'I don't want to push my luck' after getting base adjusted slightly

failure_patterns.pattern: Evaluating Canadian city offers on gross salary alone without adjusting for provincial tax differences
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Gross salary is the visible number; provincial tax rates require a separate calculation that candidates don't bother to do at decision time
failure_patterns.consequence: Systematically undervaluing Alberta offers (no provincial tax = 8–12% more take-home) and overvaluing equivalent gross salaries in Ontario or BC
warning_signs: Candidate declines Calgary offer because 'it's lower than Toronto' without doing tax-adjusted comparison
Candidate doesn't ask about provincial tax implications when comparing multi-city offers

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting a Research Scientist / Vector Institute postdoc-adjacent role without understanding the compensation gap vs. industry
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Academic prestige and research affiliation make low-compensation roles feel like career investments; candidates don't calculate the $60K–$90K postdoc vs. $120K–$200K industry researcher gap
failure_patterns.consequence: Forgoing $30K–$110K annually relative to industry researcher roles at Vector-affiliated companies doing equivalent work
warning_signs: Candidate accepts 'research track' framing without asking whether the role has industry or academic compensation structure
Candidate doesn't compare Vector-affiliated company researcher comp vs. Vector Institute direct compensation

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you comparing this offer to Canadian market data or US market data?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate's reference point is calibrated to the Canadian market or will systematically mislead their negotiation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Which Canadian sources are you using — Robert Half Canada, Glassdoor CA, or something else?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You need to recalibrate entirely — US benchmarks are 25–40% higher and will cause you to either lose the offer or leave money on the table

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this offer from a FAANG Canada employer (Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Shopify) or a mid-tier / enterprise Canadian company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether to benchmark against FAANG Canada ranges (20–40% above Robert Half) or against the broad Robert Half / Glassdoor CA market ranges
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are you negotiating RSU grants and vesting schedule, or only base salary?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Focus on signing bonus as the primary negotiating lever since base bands tend to be narrower and more fixed

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the offer include RSUs or stock options, and do you know the 4-year vesting value?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands their actual total compensation or is only evaluating base salary
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you compared the RSU grant size to benchmarks for your level at this company?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Request the full equity breakdown immediately — at senior levels RSUs can represent 30–50% of total comp and are negotiable

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the role in Alberta (Calgary/Edmonton) or in Ontario/BC?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate needs to apply an 8–12% take-home premium to Alberta gross salary before comparing to Ontario/BC offers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you calculated the after-tax take-home difference, not just gross salary comparison?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you aware that Ontario and BC provincial income taxes will reduce take-home by 8–12% more than an equivalent Alberta salary?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you asked about the signing bonus yet?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has left the most immediately negotiable component of a Canadian tech offer unclaimed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What number did you ask for, and what was the response?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask before you accept — signing bonuses are expected to be requested at Canadian tech companies even when base is fixed

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you an international candidate comparing a Canadian offer to a US offer, and what is your immigration pathway in each country?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is factoring in immigration stability premium (Canadian PR in 1–2 years vs. H-1B uncertainty + potential 134-year green card wait) into the compensation comparison
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How are you weighting immigration security vs. the compensation gap — especially at FAANG level where the US gap is severe?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Even if both offers are from Canadian employers, understanding your PR timeline affects how much negotiating risk you can afford to take

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your years of experience, and what level/title is the role being offered?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is being correctly leveled — mis-leveling down costs $25K–$40K annually in Canada
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the offered base salary align with Robert Half Canada ranges for that experience tier in your city?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Map your YOE to the junior/mid/senior bands and verify the offer falls within the correct range before negotiating the number

industry_realities.common_belief: Salary negotiation advice and benchmarks are globally applicable — the same tactics and numbers work everywhere
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian tech salaries are 25–40% lower in USD terms than US equivalents, and the compensation structure is fundamentally different (base-heavy, less equity, narrower negotiating bands). US-calibrated advice actively misleads Canadian job seekers.
industry_realities.implication: Always source Canadian-specific benchmarks (Robert Half Canada, Glassdoor CA) before any Canadian negotiation — treat US data as a separate market entirely

industry_realities.common_belief: When a Canadian employer says 'the band is set,' negotiation is over
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian employers typically have less flexibility on base salary (3–10% negotiating band) but retain meaningful discretion on signing bonuses, which are expected to be asked for at tech companies
industry_realities.implication: When base is closed, immediately pivot to asking for a signing bonus rather than accepting the conversation as finished

industry_realities.common_belief: Robert Half Canada salary ranges represent the ceiling for what you can negotiate
industry_realities.actual_reality: Robert Half ranges represent the broad market including non-tech employers. FAANG Canada (Amazon, Google, Shopify) pays 20–40% above Robert Half ranges, with senior SWE total comp reaching $175K–$260K+ CAD
industry_realities.implication: Use Robert Half as a floor benchmark to avoid being underpaid, but calibrate upward to FAANG Canada-specific data when negotiating with major tech employers

industry_realities.common_belief: A higher gross salary in Toronto always means more money than a lower gross salary in Calgary
industry_realities.actual_reality: Alberta has no provincial income tax, so a Calgary gross salary yields approximately 8–12% more take-home than the same gross in Ontario or BC
industry_realities.implication: Always compute after-tax take-home when comparing multi-city Canadian offers — do not compare gross salary figures across provinces without adjusting for provincial tax

industry_realities.common_belief: The Canada–US compensation gap is modest and mainly affects senior roles
industry_realities.actual_reality: For early/mid career in non-FAANG US, the gap is 20–40% and meaningful but not catastrophic. For FAANG: a senior SWE earns $150K–$220K CAD ($110K–$161K USD) in Canada vs. $250K–$400K USD at US FAANG — a gap that compounds severely over a career
industry_realities.implication: The decision to pursue a Canadian vs. US career path is a high-stakes financial decision that should be made with full awareness of the FAANG-level gap; immigration stability is a real but quantifiable offset

industry_realities.common_belief: A Vector Institute research role and an industry researcher role at a Vector-affiliated company are comparable in compensation
industry_realities.actual_reality: Vector Institute direct (academic/postdoc-adjacent) pays $60K–$90K CAD. Industry researcher roles at Vector-affiliated companies pay $120K–$200K CAD — a gap of $30K–$110K+ annually for potentially equivalent work
industry_realities.implication: Candidates should explicitly clarify whether a research role has academic or industry compensation structure before accepting; the affiliation name alone does not determine pay level

industry_realities.common_belief: Statistics Canada data is the most reliable source for tech salary benchmarks
industry_realities.actual_reality: Statistics Canada SEPH data is based on payroll records and systematically undercounts tech compensation. Robert Half Canada and Glassdoor CA are more accurate for individual negotiation benchmarks.
industry_realities.implication: Do not use Statistics Canada SEPH as your primary negotiation reference; use it only for occupational trend analysis and rely on Robert Half Canada and Glassdoor CA for actual benchmarks

industry_realities.common_belief: Pay transparency laws don't matter until they're fully in force
industry_realities.actual_reality: BC and Ontario pay transparency legislation (effective Jan 2026 for Ontario employers with 25+ employees) will require posted salary ranges, eliminating information asymmetry that currently disadvantages candidates
industry_realities.implication: Early-complying employers already post ranges; candidates should ask for the salary band directly even before legislation takes full effect, since many employers will now share it

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Uses whatever salary data appears first in Google search results, which is typically US-centric (levels.fyi, Glassdoor US) — does not distinguish between US and Canadian markets
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Immediately identifies Canadian-specific sources (Robert Half Canada, Glassdoor CA, National Job Bank) and understands that US benchmarks are a different dataset requiring explicit adjustment
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Miscalibrated anchors either cost the candidate the offer (too high) or thousands of dollars annually (too low)

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Focuses exclusively on base salary as the negotiation target; accepts outcome when told 'the band is set'
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Treats base, signing bonus, RSU grant size, vesting schedule, and RRSP match as separate negotiation levers — pivots to signing bonus when base is closed
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Leaving signing bonus unasked at Canadian tech companies is free money foregone; RSU negotiation at senior levels can represent 30–50% of total comp

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Evaluates offers based on base salary number alone; treats equity and benefits as secondary or unclear
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Calculates 4-year total comp including RSU vesting, signing bonus, RRSP match, and after-tax take-home adjusted for province
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Two offers with the same base salary can differ by 30–50% in actual 4-year value depending on equity and provincial tax structure

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Compares gross salary numbers across Canadian cities at face value; assumes higher gross = better offer
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Adjusts for Alberta's provincial income tax absence (8–12% take-home premium) and Montreal's lower COL offset when comparing offers across provinces
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Candidates who don't make this adjustment systematically undervalue Calgary offers and potentially make suboptimal relocation decisions

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Canada vs. US career path decision
junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Focuses on immediate salary comparison; may either overvalue US FAANG comp without accounting for immigration risk, or undervalue it without realizing the magnitude of the long-term gap
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Frames Canada vs. US as a multi-variable expected value calculation: compensation gap (severe at FAANG level) vs. immigration stability premium (Canadian PR in 1–2 years vs. H-1B + potential 134-year GC wait)
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: This is potentially a multi-million dollar career decision; treating it as a simple salary comparison misses the immigration stability variable that meaningfully changes the calculus for international candidates

junior_vs_senior_signals.junior_pattern: Treats all tech employer salary benchmarks as interchangeable; applies Robert Half ranges uniformly across FAANG Canada and mid-tier employers
junior_vs_senior_signals.senior_pattern: Maintains separate mental benchmarks for FAANG Canada (Amazon, Google, Shopify — 20–40% above Robert Half) vs. broad market employers, and adjusts negotiation expectations accordingly
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Using Robert Half ranges at a FAANG Canada negotiation means anchoring $20K–$50K below the employer's actual pay ceiling for the role
